claims.text: Adding a controlled Y2O3 nanoparticle dispersion to MoNbTaW by mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering will increase yield strength relative to conventionally processed MoNbTaW without oxide dispersion.
The Y2O3 dispersion will improve creep resistance relative to conventionally processed MoNbTaW without oxide dispersion.
The Y2O3-dispersed alloy will preserve thermal stability.
The Y2O3-dispersed alloy will preserve irradiation stability.
Mechanical alloying, spark plasma sintering, and annealing at 800–1200 °C under inert atmosphere will produce a uniform oxide dispersion.
The resulting Y2O3 nanoparticles will be located both at grain boundaries and within the MoNbTaW matrix.
The dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will remain thermally stable.
Y2O3 nanoparticles impede dislocation motion and thereby provide dispersion strengthening.
Y2O3 nanoparticles act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
Defect-sink behavior of the nanoparticles will mitigate irradiation-induced defect accumulation.
The treated alloy will exhibit a statistically significant reduction in irradiation-induced defect density relative to the untreated alloy.
The benefits depend on optimization of nanoparticle size, distribution, and volume fraction.
Exceptionally high irradiation fluence or thermal cycling beyond the tested annealing range may diminish the benefits.
Poorly optimized nanoparticle parameters may cause embrittlement.
